subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: Should OpenClaw approve a bounded per-reviewer-instance exact-input memo for low-risk model-backed exec reviewer decisions on repeated identical exec requests?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but reusing a prior model verdict changes the exec approval boundary, so cache lifetime, key shape, cached outcome set, and sibling helper scope require maintainer intent before merge.

options.title: Approve bounded exact-input memo
options.body: Land one linked PR after it has redacted configured-run proof, with a per-reviewer-instance cache keyed by the full reviewed input and no durable approval reuse.

options.title: Require broader helper coverage
options.body: Keep the fix blocked until plugin/app-server helper paths either reuse reviewer lifetime or are explicitly documented as out of scope.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Decline reviewer memoization and accept repeated model cost to preserve one fresh model review per exec request.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded exact-input memo
recommendation.body: Land one linked PR after it has redacted configured-run proof, with a per-reviewer-instance cache keyed by the full reviewed input and no durable approval reuse.

likelyOwner.reason: The normalized exec auto-mode commit introduced the shared reviewer and approval semantics being changed.
